Messages.Author: nys...@cs.com
Messages.Body:
There are a number of of cards, available to vampires, that seem to
represent the ability to operate by sunlight: Dawn Operation, Daring
the Dawn, Day Operation, superior Beast Meld, Alpha Glint (I'm not
entirely sure of the thematic significance of the last two). Three of
these (Daring the Dawn, Day Operation, superior Beast Meld) make
actions unblockable to vampires. Dawn Operation permite vampires to
block, but at a price. Alpha Glint is a "combat ends" mechanism.

It has always seemed to me somewhat incongruous to me that no similar
effects have been incorporated for the benefit of allies.

This is precisely why, thematically, Vampires traditionally employ
ghouls and hell hounds -- to stop those pesky mortals who come
creeping around in the daytime. Most people I know regard Hell Hounds
as wallpaper -- too expensive to play, and too fragile to block
vampires. But if day-operating allies were more common, then
creatures like Hell Hounds would make much more strategic sense. They
may be too fragile to block Beast the Leatherface, but not necessarily
too fragile to block Jake Washington or Loyal Street Gang (also never
played).

People concerned that the Imbued are overpowered will of course now
howl in panic at my evil proposal to make them even more powerful.
But in recent discussions of the imbued, I suggested a "fix" to make
them more burnable in combat (not because I thought them too powerful,
but because I thought this more thematically appropriate for mortals,
and also more "fun"), and it was protested that it would make them too
weak. But why not have thematically appropriate weaknesses balanced
by thematically appropriate strengths?

To clarify, I am not proposing a new cardless rule, just cards usable
by allies. I'm not going to propose any specific card designs.
Appropriate limitations can be found if felt necessary to prevent
their being too powerful: (ie. Vampires with fortitude might be less
affected; acting allies, deprived of the support of a Methuselah who
has gone to bed, might be unable to replace cards until the end of the
action; cards might be limited to specific kinds of actions rather
than being all purpose like the vampire-specific cards; actions might
be at -1 stealth, etc. etc.)

Type: Event

a Time counter to this card. When there are more than 4 counters on
this card, any ally reduced to 0 life is removed from the game. When
there are fewer than 5 counters on this card, allies have +1 bleed,
and when a vampire blocks an acting ally, all damage in the resulting
combat is aggravated. Burn all counters on this card when it has more
than 9. Any player may discard another The Witching Hour as a discard
phase action to add 5 counters to this card.

I have to agree somewhat with Dave, though he may overstate the point.
In any case, Day Operation style effects for the Imbued and other
allies would likely be horrible for game balance, and it's well
established that theme is not a good reason to make poor design
choices. The suggestion that players could add cards to their decks to
counter such effects is ludicrous. It is already far from possible to
defend against all the available delivery systems and still have room
to do anything.

Additionally, one can certainly invent a thematic explanation for why
allies acting in the day aren't unblockable by vampires, because one
can pretty much make up a thematic explanation for anything (which is
precisely why thematic design choices and arguments are fruitless).
Since VTES is a game about vampires, we can assume that anything an
ally does is in some way meddling in the affairs of vampires, which is
very likely to entail some activity at night for information
gathering, social engineering, etc. Even if a mortal attempts to hack
computers during the day, he might have to spend some time out and
about at night to find the necessary information. Vampires are able to
slip by defenses during the day because they already have all of that
information, and they can quickly perform day time missions that
require it. Moreover, everyone expects mortals to be active during the
day. When vampires do it it's particularly surprising, so it is far
more likely to provide an effective form of cover. Finally, on a
related point, there is no reason to think that an ally's actions all
occur within a short time frame. Even when an ally is doing something
that doesn't need to involve vampires or their resources (such as
learning a power), it might take several days and tipped off vampires
could intervene in the night times that come between them.

Can we please stop all this theme nonsense? VTES is a strategic card
game, and while I do enjoy the theme (I'm a former V:tM player), the
card strategy should always come first.

Messages.Author: Thrall of Arika
Messages.Body:
And who's to say that the allies aren't acting during the day for many
actions? An unblocked computer hack could easily be thought of being
done during the day, with the prey's vampires unable to react, only to
'wake' in the evening to find that their finacial records have been
hacked and a large sum of money disappeared (Pool loss).

Even a vampire attempting to block and failing could be though of
trying to stop an ally, but dawn breaks, preventing the vampire from
intercepting.

But if such cards do come into existence, I see no reason why they
should be limited to mortals and animals. Vampires are pretty much the
only ones with the limitation. Mages are just Awakened mortals, ghouls
are mortals who subsist on vampire blood to make them supernaturally
stronger. Werewolves, zombies, wraiths, changelings, mummies ... all
work fine in sunlight as well as darkness. I personally don't see a
problem with such a card, giving appropriate limitations/costs.

Now whether such a card would make the Imbued unbalanced is up for
another debate, which can only really happen when such a card is
developed.

Chris, Thrall of Arika

That's one way to look at things, but it doesn't necessarily mean
that's the way it is. Yes, humans by default aren't a nocturnal
species, but we do spend a lot of our waking hours during the night.
Heck, it gets dark sometime after 5 nowadays, so you're looking at a
good 6 hours of free time that a mortal could be busily at work
foiling the plans of your prey. If every bleed was a daytime bleed,
how are vampires stopping so many? Plus, at night, it's a lot easier
to skulk around and sabotage some part of your prey's resources (aka
bleed for pool damage), less chance of being caught by other mortals,
or seen in general, as well as less likelihood of innocents getting
caught in the cross-fire (if you're one to care about such things).

Hunters often act at night, trying to trace movements of vampires.
It's a lot easier to find your target when it's moving and acting that
it is when it's holed up in its unknown lair.

Civil workers have day jobs, and while they can sometimes act on your
behalf during that time, they often have other, mundane affairs that
need to be taken care of. If you continually abuse their position
during their normal working hours, you risk them losing their
position, and thus their usefulness.

Personally, I see most if not all actions taking place during the
night, which explains how vampires can actively attempt to stop
whatever actions an ally takes. If all ally actions were meant to be
during the day, then there should be default conditions to reflect
this, making it harder for a vampire to intercept. If actions go
unblocked (especially with no attempts), then it could more easily be
thought of as a day-time action.

I don't see why vampires have the ability to use daytime to their
advantage, but not allies, both thematically and by card mechanics.

Chris, Thrall of Arika

Messages.Author: Hodgestar
Messages.Body:
On Nov 6, 4:40 am, nyst...@cs.com wrote:
> It has always seemed to me somewhat incongruous to me that no similar
> effects have been incorporated for the benefit of allies.

Thematically I can't see any mortal ally conducting Computer Hacking
during the day time. In fact, are there any humans in the World of
Darkness who habitually get up before the late afternoon? Certainly
there weren't many in the campaigns I played in. :)

With this in mind, I propose:

Caffeine Operation
Action Modifier
Only usable at the end of a successful action. Untap the acting minion
and put this card on them. If the action was Computer Hacking the
minion may bleed again with Computer Hacking this turn. The minion
with this card does not untap as normal and cannot block or play
reaction cards. Burn this card at the end of your next untap phase. A
minion may play only one Caffeine Operation each turn.

I considered whether this should be restricted to mortal allies only.
I don't know what the effects of caffeine on vampires and werewolves
are -- and how would wraiths even get the caffeine into their systems?
The "does not untap" is of course irrelevant to Baali, but I suppose
looking great after pulling an all-nighter is just one of the many
advantages of selling one's soul. :)

Another possibility is:

Early Riser
Action
Put this card on a mortal ally. This ally has 0 bleed and cannot be
blocked by vampires. Vampires cannot play action modifiers while this
ally is acting. This ally cannot take the action Computer Hacking.

The 0 bleed is because nothing that happens before noon can really be
important. Vampires cannot play action modifiers like Cloak the
Gathering and Hidden Lurker because, like all sensible people, they
are asleep in their coffins.

Schiavo
Simon

No, never said that a vampire couldn't be effective during the day
(though it's not an easy thing for them, they do suffer from an
unnatural lethargy during the day). But a vampire's network works for
them, not for you (unless it is represented by additional cards in
play, such as the pet Hell Hounds). In the end, though, it's hard to
abstract away an actual block/combat from anything other than the
actual vampire combating the ally. This works fine for directed
actions against the vampire (i.e. the ally crept into the home to do
some serious damage, and the vampire awoke to confront the intruder).
But it makes it more difficult to believe that a vampire got up in the
middle of the day, high-tailed it across town and intercepting the
offending ally, all while avoided the deadly sunlight.

I would also be very against making any 'daytime' cards allowing for
unblockable actions. I would be more inclined to follow along with
Dawn Operation, where damage is aggravated, or even just that the
reacting vampire must spend blood to block or attempt to (using the
blood to awaken themselves earlier, which I believe is an actual
ability in the RPG). Or simpler effects like giving -1 intercept to
vampires/monsters. But then having the card so diluted and matching
other cards already, there seems little point to making it.

It's about keeping options open, rather than automatically saying 'no'
and closing off potential avenues. That being said, allies have
unblockable card access already. Project, Incriminating Videotape,
Memories, etc.

Perhaps a daytime card for some other aspect of play. Daytime Assault
making damage in combat with a vampire aggravated. Clearing the Rats
Nest doing a point of damage to all members of a certain clan.

Of course, empowering allies against should also lead to cards
empowering vampires against allies. A balance has to be found that
keeps the game fresh and giving chances to explore new ways of doing
things, while maintaining game mechanics balance so that one archetype
isn't overpowering any other consistently.

Chris, Thrall of Arika

Messages.Author: Seamus.O...@gmail.com

On Nov 8, 12:44 am, nyst...@cs.com wrote:

> Right. Which was why I did not bother to suggest a specific design.
> I'm sure the design team could do a better job than I could. I was
> just throwing out a wish-list of a theme I'd like to see explored.

Two ideas that occur to me on reading this are:

Flagrant Disregard for the Law.
Action modifier.
Only usable as the action is announced. Requires an ally. Vampires
cannot block this action. After resolving this action put this card on
the acting ally, this ally cannot block or take actions. Any minion
may burn this card as an action that costs 1 pool.

Friends in High Places.
Action modifier.
Only usable as the action is announced. Requires an ally. If this
action is blocked all damage in the resulting combat is aggravated.
Cost: 1 pool

Thematically the first represents your guy getting arrested and having
to be bailed out, the second represents spreading bribes around in
order to not get arrested.
Costs and such can obviously be tweaked, but I don't think either of
them would be inherently game breaking.

Seamus.

It's like the old axiom says, you get what you pay for. In my
thematics, I don't see influencing a vampire to mean that you totally
control them 100%. You are investing in what they are willing to do
for you. Vampires all have their own plans and machinations. If I was
a vampire, I may be influenced to assist some old Methuselah, but I'd
be damned if I would turn over my entire resource network to them.
Perhaps I want to keep my Hell Hounds and use them to protect my own
interest (outside of game). But if the Methuselah sweetens the pot
(say 2 more Pool) well, I could probably be convinced to bring in one
of my Hell Hounds to assist in their endeavours (recruit Hell Hound).

Now being the Methuselah, if some 'lackey' vampire of mine got found
out and attacked in their haven, well, I'd expend some resources to
assist them, sure. I've invested a fair bit of my own resources in
them. But eventually it would come to a point to cut my losses and
abandon them (they get burned). If the hapless lackey was too greedy
to give me control over more of their own minions and resouces to the
point where they bungle using them themselves, well, perhaps they
deserved the stake after all.

> I mean if the vampire works for you, and their resources works for
> them why their resources are not considered to work for you too, if
> those are part of the reasons why you wanted to recruit them?

There's a line where control over assets is either the Methuselah or
the Vampire. Now I may invest in a sweet new top-of-the-line laptop
for my lackey, but I'm not going to sit there and tell them how to go
about hacking and destroying the finanacial records of my opponent
(Bleed), that's up to the lackey. It's up to them to use their own
knowledge and sources to get the job done.

> > Of course, empowering allies against should also lead to cards
> > empowering vampires against allies. A balance has to be found that
> > keeps the game fresh and giving chances to explore new ways of doing
> > things, while maintaining game mechanics balance so that one archetype

> things that hose vampires and they do well. Vampires, on the other
> hand, have to pack everything to defend against agg. damage, against
> MoM, against Events, and now would have to defend against daylights
> tricks.

Imbued are affected by numerous events. It's just that there are a
number of them that specifically only affect vampires.

Aggravated Damage affects Imbued just fine, it's just that they are
not any more particularly vulnerable to it. In fact, you could say
they suffer more. 1 aggravated damage just sends a vampire to Torpor,
it causes the loss of 1 life for an Imbued.

The only 'problem' I see is the difficulty in burning Imbued, compared
to other minions, Vampires and library Allies alike. I'm starting to
like the idea of burning Convictions for excess damage done in combat,
representing the Imbued's loss of faith and determination when finally
faced with the true horror that some vampires can unleash. If they
don't have the conviction, then they burn. Would certainly need to be
play-tested some, I don't have the experience against or with using
the Imbued to know if this would shift the balance to making them
unplayable. But at the moment seems to be a reasonable compromise
between the 'Imbued rule all' and the 'Imbued are cake' camps.

As to what vampires have to defend against, well, they had to defend
against all that before. Memories has been around for a while, and was
a staple in ally decks before the Imbued came about. Aggravated damage
is always a worry, and clans like Gangrel and Tzimisce were far more
effective in dishing it out. Events were a problem before Imbued as
well. And vampires have their own daytime tricks already, not that
these is much that can be done to 'defend' against it. There's no
'make something unblockable blockable' card beyond those that cancel
cards (i.e. Direct Intervention).

Chris, Thrall of Arika

not worth the risk investing in them beyond their base abilities.
Imbued can afford to load up on equipment on cards, because there is
little fear of losing them.

As to needing extra defences against them, I don't agree. You're more
likely to be bled at +bleed and +stealth by a vampire than you are an
Imbued, so if you're not already prepared for that contigency, it's
certainly not the fault of the Imbued player or Imbued mechanics.
There's little Imbued can do that could not already be replicated by
vampire decks. Vampire decks could be tuned to bleed at stealth, to

It's odd, as the Imbued are at the same time far more resilient and
far more fragile than vampires. Most combat will just send them to the
Incapacitated region, with little fear of losing the minion. And yet,
one undodged Mercy of Seth means a fully loaded up Imbued goes poof.
Similarly burning a vampire takes a lot more setup than this.

I do agree that something should be done, as the typically combative
disciplines have a mystifying inability to deal with allies, while
typically non-combative disciplines have aces up their sleeves to
easily deal with them. Either through development of the base rules
(i.e. burning conviction for excess damage), or producing cards
effective against allies for these combat disciplines. Perhaps
something like a Potence strike Break the Neck, sending an opposing
vampire to torpor, or burning an ally.
